Our story, in chapters

Every journey begins somewhere.

Ours begins with a door that's open, a chair that's free, and people who understand — because many of us have been there ourselves.

A warm welcome — from the moment you arrive
Chapter 01

01 — A safe space

Before anything can change, a person needs somewhere they feel safe. We offer a safe space for anyone experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity — somewhere you can sit down, take a breath, and talk to someone who will treat you with dignity, not judgement.

You don't need to have everything figured out before you come to us. Come as you are, and take things one step at a time, at your own pace.

“Safety isn't a service. It's the ground everything else grows from.”
A fresh start — keys in hand
Chapter 02

02 — A way forward

From that first safe moment, we walk alongside you. A dedicated case worker helps you make sense of your options — housing, health and the practical steps in between — and turns an overwhelming situation into a plan you can actually follow.

And when the keys are finally in your hand, we don't disappear. Our support continues for as long as it takes to make a house feel like home.

“Nobody should have to find their way back alone.”
How we work

Our Approach

Three simple commitments shape everything we do — early help, steady support, and the strength of people who understand.

01

Intervention

Early support to help people facing homelessness or housing insecurity — stepping in quickly, before a difficult situation becomes a crisis.

02

Continued Support

Practical, personalised assistance throughout the journey towards stability — one named case worker, one plan, and support that stays.

03

Peer Support

Building meaningful connections through shared experiences, understanding and encouragement — because people who have lived it can light the way.

What we offer

Services & Support

Practical help and human support, under one roof — so you never have to retell your story to a stranger twice.

i.

Housing and Homelessness Support

Help finding safe accommodation, understanding your housing rights, and support to keep a tenancy once you have one.

ii.

Mental Health Counselling

Confidential counselling with qualified mental health counsellors, in a calm space and at a pace that feels right for you.

iii.

Nursing and Healthcare

On-site nursing and healthcare support, from wound care and health checks to help registering with a GP and getting to appointments.

iv.

Dedicated Case Workers

One named case worker who knows your situation, coordinates your support and stands in your corner at every step.

v.

Ongoing Personal Support

Continued one-to-one support after the crisis has passed — budgeting, paperwork, confidence and the everyday things that rebuild a life.

vi.

Peer Support Community

A welcoming community of people with shared experience — groups, activities and friendships that remind you you're not alone.

The founder & our story

30 Years of Experience. 367 Lives Changed. One Mission.

Our founder has spent 30 years working in the homelessness sector — on the streets, in shelters and alongside the people too often overlooked. That frontline experience is backed by a Law Degree and a Master's degree in the field, bringing together compassion and a deep understanding of housing rights.

Over three decades, they have personally helped 367 people move away from street homelessness — not through grand gestures, but through patience, persistence and the belief that everyone deserves a safe place to call home.

YOUR CHARITY NAME was founded on everything those years taught: that early help changes outcomes, that support must continue beyond the crisis, and that people who have lived it are often the best guides back.

30years in the sector
367lives changed
1mission — a home for everyone

It started with outreach work — walking the streets at night, learning names, building trust one conversation at a time. Again and again, the same lesson appeared: people didn't fall through the cracks because help didn't exist, but because it arrived too late, ended too soon, or asked them to start over with every new face.

So this charity was built differently. One door, open early. One case worker, who stays. Counsellors, nurses and peer supporters working as a single team around each person — for as long as it takes. Three hundred and sixty-seven people have already made that journey from the street to a home of their own. Our mission is to make sure many more can.
